items.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021
items.q: you will never remember a Beyoncé song or a Prince song.

ctx.x: In small ways yes but mostly not. And it’s much bigger than the jazz education industry, and I use that word slightly pejoratively but not entirely. It just is a way to talk about it. The only other period that I know of in which popular art seemed also to be at this kind of high level is the period of Elizabethan theater. You know I’m talking about the period starting with Scott Joplin and Jelly Roll Morton and John Philip Sousa, that’s the late nineteenth century, and carrying through Louis Armstrong and the…

undeveloped people with money in their pockets became the target of the market machinery. And their music, their adolescent music and adolescent musical ideas, undeveloped musical ideas, took over and marginalized everything else. And that is, and now we’re in that system and have been there since roughly the mid-60s. It’s hard to put a date on it but, or the late 60s. And now I think we’re in a much more normal situation in which good cultural things are subsidized by institutions of educated and basically…
I don’t disagree with you but we probably could find people who do.
